law: REGISTRATION of E-Q37 — THE PHRASING-SENSITIVITY CURVE (ORCH-R28 lane T19-c): the E-Q34 AM1 receipt (one reworded anchor question moved noul mass 0.18 = 2x the version-drift band) systematized. How much mass does QUESTION phrasing move, as a function of edit TYPE? Four treatments x the frozen 8-record subset, question-side transforms only (the record texts byte-identical): T0 the anchor (byte-identical standard map), T1 synonym-swap (light lexical), T2 syntactic-reorder (same words, clause order flipped), T3 role-reframe (same semantics, auditor framing). The curve quantifies the replication tolerance any future question-map reuse must declare.
provenance_of_the_question: The r27 close-out registration: 'the phrasing-sensitivity curve: how much mass does sentence shape move, systematically (the E-Q34 AM1 receipt at scale).' The phrasing law (byte-identity, not semantic identity, is the replication requirement) currently rests on n=1; this lane gives it a distribution.

design_frozen.treatments: All transforms applied to the 8 REAL question texts only (decoys ride along byte-identical in every call — in-call floor check). T0 ANCHOR: the byte-identical standard 8-question map (the E-Q22 map). T1 SYNONYM-SWAP: per question, exactly two content words replaced by near-synonyms ('substantively concern' -> 'meaningfully engage'; 'Judge whether' -> 'Assess whether'; 'about this concern' -> 'on this matter'). T2 SYNTACTIC-REORDER: the same sentences with clause order flipped ('Judge whether the record is about this concern. Record: does it substantively concern X?' -> 'Is the record about this concern? The record: does it substantively concern X. Judge.'). T3 ROLE-REFRAME: auditor framing ('You are auditing a sealed experiment record. Determine whether it substantively concerns X.'). The four treatment texts frozen here as templates, applied by explicit loop.
design_frozen.calls: One batched 12-question call per record per treatment: 8 records x 4 treatments = 32 calls, jev-latest, AS-SAID rows, resume law. The T0 calls ARE the in-run anchor (same session, same everything).
design_frozen.measures: M1 per (record, axis): |p_T - p_T0| for T in {T1,T2,T3} — the movement distribution per treatment (median, p90, max, % > 0.10 band). M2 SHAPE PRESERVATION: Spearman(8-axis profile under T, profile under T0) per record — does the RANK survive when the MASS does not? M3 AXIS SUSCEPTIBILITY: per axis, mean movement across records — is there a consistent per-axis phrasing susceptibility profile? M4 FAMILY EFFECT: does movement differ by record family? M5 the decoy floor under each treatment (the canaries must stay dead under paraphrase — injection resistance vs paraphrase are different properties).

floors.F1: the four treatment templates frozen here, byte-identical application by explicit loop; no post-hoc edits
floors.F2: record texts byte-identical across all treatments (question-side only)
floors.F3: one batched call per record per treatment, all 12 answers present, p in [0,1]
floors.F4: T0 must replicate the sealed E-Q22 vectors within the 0.10 band on >= 7 of 8 records (the anchor check; a failed anchor fails the lane)
floors.F5: movement measured against the IN-RUN T0 anchor (not the sealed vectors) for all treatment comparisons

hypotheses.H1_movement: at least one treatment moves > 0.10 on >= 25% of (record, axis) pairs — phrasing variance is a real component (the phrasing law at scale)
hypotheses.H2_shape: median Spearman(profile_T, profile_T0) >= 0.8 across all treatments — the profile SHAPE is phrasing-robust even when MASS is not
hypotheses.H3_susceptibility: per-axis susceptibility ranks correlate across treatments (Spearman >= 0.6 between at least two treatment pairs) — susceptibility is an AXIS property, not noise
hypotheses.C35: phrasing variance is bounded and structured — mass moves beyond the band (H1) but the shape survives (H2); LIVES iff H1 AND H2

predictions.P1: T3 (role-reframe) moves the most mass (the persona shift reads as a different question); T1 (synonym) the least
predictions.P2: movement concentrates on mid-mass axes (0.2-0.6) — extreme masses are pinned by the record text, ambiguous ones float with phrasing
predictions.P3: shape Spearman >= 0.9 for T1, in [0.7, 0.9] for T2/T3
predictions.P4: the decoy floor stays <= 0.05 under ALL treatments (dead axes stay dead — canary immunity to paraphrase)
predictions.P5: P6_null (the refuted-hypothesis axis) is the most phrasing-susceptible real axis (its concept text is the most abstract)

falsifier: ANY of F1-F5 breached; a treatment template edited after registration; movement computed against sealed vectors instead of the in-run anchor; the anchor band stretched.
budget: 32 typesafe calls. Part of the r28 round budget.
